scope: Optimized final rendering, matched DR0 raster and echo, four physical-input cohorts, drag, passive copy/IRQ costs, and extracted OF816 previews. Existing raw/optimized compiler-boundary and deeper fault evidence is reused from DR1-DR6.
measurement_limits: Scanout observations are upper bounds, at most one PAL frame late.
Copy submission CPU includes setup, upload, launch and return; upload is not separately timed.
Launch to IRQ idle observation includes DMA plus IRQ latency; exact hardware BUSY-edge timing is unavailable.
Settled scene timings include all request/repair/caret work and two PAL settling frames, not only DMA.
Cache comparisons include capture and retained fallback; no universal caching speedup is claimed.

open_targets: Pointer p95: idle 46.41 ms >40, scrolling 61.31 ms >60, two-client 65.86 ms >60. All pointer maxima, button maxima and sub-ms sampler-gap gates pass.
Drag release repair: idle maximum 299.54 ms; scrolling 1181.92 ms; disk 1422.43 ms, all above 250 ms.
Outline p95 exceeds 40/60 ms in all three drag cohorts; idle/scroll maxima also exceed 60/100 ms.
Some retained widget/odd-clip scenes remain multi-second despite warm snapshot reuse. Timing acceptance is not achieved.
follow_up: Instrument release-to-copy admission, geometry commit, exposure repair and first scanout in the same physical drag run. Current copy stage costs are small relative to end-to-end delay; do not attribute loaded repair solely to DMA.
Bound retained preparation and improve presenter scheduling/input service at existing quiescent boundaries before reducing protection or increasing list size.
Reduce setup and glyph replay for odd clipped/fragmented fallback and complex widget focus rebuilds. Preserve exact visibility and the fixed latency targets.
Retest the same four input and three drag cohorts only after a focused performance change.
